root_idea.summary: The root develops several related orientations: a pattern or visible mark, deficiency or incompleteness, and whiteness associated with distinction, excellence, or nobility. In the Quranic deception vocabulary, the notion of being folded away from the true state develops into misleading appearances and false hopes.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence connects creases, original patterns, and visible marks with forms and boundaries; from another branch it connects shortfall with deficient milk, incomplete acts, and uncertain transactions; the whiteness branch extends to excellence and eminence. The deception vocabulary is explained through the idea of causing someone to follow a misleading appearance or vain prospect.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A distinct Quran-attested Form I verb, normalized to its Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
A distinct Quran-attested nominal form meaning a deceiver or deceiving power.
A distinct Quran-attested verbal noun or abstract noun meaning deception, delusion, or false appearance.

senses.definition: To deceive or beguile, inducing a person to desire what is vain or false and thereby leading him into error, disobedience, or misplaced security.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use: a person, worldly life, or another agent deceives someone. In the Quranic construction مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ, the deception is understood as making the addressee disregard what is incumbent, feel secure from punishment, or become emboldened to disobey.

senses.definition: A deceiver: one who beguiles people with false promises or hopes, especially the devil as the archetypal deceiver.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage the form may refer specifically to the devil, understood as the most pernicious of deceivers; it can also function as a substantivized epithet.

senses.definition: A deceiving worldly power or advantage, especially worldly life and its attractions when they give rise to false hopes.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passages concerning this form, the expression is also interpreted as the worldly life or worldly advantages insofar as they deceive; this is a distinct referential use from the personal deceiver.

senses.definition: Deception or delusion: a false or vain promise, appearance, or prospect by which a person is misled.
senses.usage_conditions: The form denotes deception as a condition, means, or result. Quranic contexts include Satanic or human promises, misleading appearances, and the deceptive attractions of worldly life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a young bird with the beak; of a male pigeon, to feed its female with the beak. Figuratively, to nourish or instruct someone with knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative instructional use is an extension of the bird-feeding construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be inexperienced or ignorant in practical affairs, or to act in a youthful or childish manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use applied to a man, youth, or young person; the sources also mention acting childishly after previously possessing sound judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become white or acquire a white mark on the forehead or face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse or camel, and of the face when it becomes white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become eminent or noble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate intransitive use reported of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a grapevine, to become tall quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour water into a receptacle, watering-trough, or waterskin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the imperative construction used for filling a trough or skin by putting it into water and throwing water into it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To expose oneself or one's property to perdition, destruction, loss, or other serious risk without knowing the outcome; to endanger or hazard oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II is used with the reflexive phrase بِـنَفْسِهِ and may also take property as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mark a horse with a white forehead blaze or other غُرَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II use concerning the animal's facial marking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a child's teeth, to show their points, emerge, or begin to grow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The imagery is connected with the whiteness of the teeth becoming visible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of birds, to desire or attempt flight and raise their wings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized inchoative or preparatory use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a waterskin or water-container.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II transitive use distinct from the Form I expression for pouring water into a receptacle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to become scant or deficient in milk, especially to draw up her milk after previously yielding it freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The use can describe withholding milk after delayed milking, fright, or another cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a market, to become stagnant or dull in trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the cessation or deficiency of flow, contrasted with a market that is flourishing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a male pigeon, to feed its female with the beak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III construction concerning courtship or feeding between pigeons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To embolden or encourage someone, possibly by deceiving him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical report is attributed to an authority and accompanied by a disputed interpretation of the cited poetic line; the meaning is therefore retained with that qualification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to fall into peril, danger, jeopardy, hazard, or risk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate causative interpretation, though the source notes that it may derive from a disputed reading of the illustrative verse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become deceived or beguiled, and thereby to desire what is vain or false.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may take بِـ to indicate the thing by which one is deceived.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become negligent, inattentive, heedless, or unprepared, thinking oneself secure and therefore failing to remain on guard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the resulting state associated with being deceived or falsely secure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come upon someone when he is negligent or unprepared, or to seek to take advantage of his negligence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction distinct from the intransitive state of becoming deceived.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gargle with water or medicine, causing it to move repeatedly in the throat without ejecting it or easily swallowing it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized reduplicated verb describing reciprocal movement in the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cooking pot, to make a sound while boiling; of meat, to make a sound while broiling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An imitative or sound-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give up the spirit at death, apparently with a rattling sound in the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physiological and death-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reiterate or reverberate the voice in the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a speaker or pastor's voice and also in the reflexive form of the voice becoming reiterated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter someone by cutting the throat or to pierce the throat with a spearhead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive physical attack directed at the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break the nasal bone or the neck or mouth of a flask or bottle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized breaking use associated with the throat or opening of an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to come and go repeatedly in the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or iterative use describing repeated movement of fluid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A crease, wrinkle, fold, or pleat in skin, a garment, or cloth; by extension, the original fold or state in which something is left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes expressions for folding cloth according to its original crease and for leaving a person as he is without disclosing his condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fissure or cleft in the earth or ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal geographical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rivulet or narrow stream of water in the land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained as referring to a stream that cleaves the earth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The streaks or lines of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural or collective nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two lines along the sides of the lower part of an arrowhead or blade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized term for paired lines on the iron head of an arrow or similar implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremity or point of a tooth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported in the same lexical family as the crease and line senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food with which a bird feeds its young by its bill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A poetic figurative expression describes exhausting camels as though their bird-food had been consumed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An inexperienced, simple, or unworldly person who is ignorant of practical affairs and may act childishly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man, youth, girl, or young woman; the source also records the sense of a young woman inexperienced in matters of love.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who submits to being deceived.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal personal description, distinct from merely being inexperienced.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness or clearness of complexion; especially a white blaze or mark on the forehead or face of a horse, camel, or dog.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal marking may be a general term for different shapes and sizes of white facial marks; the expression can also describe conspicuous fairness or innocence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first appearance or commencement of a month, especially the night or first days when the new moon is seen; by extension, the beginning of Islam or of anything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is derived from the conspicuous first appearance of a white mark; the term may also denote the aspect or appearance of the new moon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The whiteness of the teeth or the first tooth to appear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily use connected with visible whiteness and emergence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The head or first emerging part of a plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed-tropical extension of the first-appearance sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The visible appearance of light, daybreak, or a spectacle that becomes manifest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of conspicuous whiteness or first appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person's face, forehead, or aspect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on the face as the conspicuous front or visible mark of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An extended washing of the fore part of the head and adjacent limbs in ablution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical ritual expression concerning the extent of washing beyond the ordinary minimum; the reported descriptions differ in the precise limbs included.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A noble, eminent, chief, or lord of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal use derived from conspicuous excellence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The best, chiefest, most precious, or most excellent part of property or goods; in a legal compensation context, a high-quality male or female slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The legal use concerning destruction of a fetus denotes a compensatory person or value; authorities differ over the exact valuation and whether whiteness is required.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Goodness and righteous conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed-tropical moral extension of the excellence or conspicuous virtue sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Negligence, inattention, inadvertence, heedlessness, or inexperience in practical affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the idiom عَلَى غِرَّةٍ, unexpectedly or on an occasion of negligence, and the related sense of inexperience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Boldness or presumptuous security against God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction غِرَّةٌ بِاللّٰهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Peril, danger, hazard, or risk arising from an uncertain outcome; a transaction in which the thing may or may not exist, or whose reality is concealed by its outward appearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is especially used in the legal expression بيع الغرر, including an unreliable sale or a bond lacking security and confidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Paucity or deficiency of a camel's milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same deficiency metaphor extends to little sleep and other forms of incompleteness, but this item records the milk sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Little or insufficient sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of deficiency or scantness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deficiency or incomplete performance in prayer or salutation, including incomplete bowing, prostration, purification, or abbreviated forms of greeting and reply.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical construction in the prohibition لا غِرَارَ في صلاة ولا تسليم; authorities report variant interpretations of the salutation clause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Haste or acting with too little consideration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for coming to or meeting someone hastily.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short stay or a small amount of time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of remaining somewhere briefly or of a period measured by comparison with a month.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way, course, mode, or manner; a repeated pattern or sequence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of arrows shot in one course, children born successively in one pattern, or structures made according to one manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The model or pattern according to which arrowheads are fashioned and straightened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical object-making use distinct from the general sense of way or manner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The point, edge, or cutting extremity of a spear, arrow, sword, or anything possessing an edge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dual may denote the two sides or edges of a blade or arrowhead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medicine or preparation with which one gargles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal instrument or preparation term, compared with words for medicines taken by other routes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man deceived into marrying a woman whom he believes to be free and discovers to be enslaved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized social application of the general sense of being deceived.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unexpectedly knowledgeable informant who can state the true condition of an affair without prior preparation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression أَنَا غَرِيرُكَ مِنْ هٰذَا الأَمْرِ, authorities also report an alternative interpretation in which the speaker is a deceived informant passing on false information.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who cautions or protects another from being deceived by someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَنَا غَرِيرُكَ مِنْهُ, literally presenting the speaker as a safeguard against that person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surety, sponsor, or guarantor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional extension of standing in place of, or being liable for, another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A life in which one is not made to live in fear or apprehension.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a secure or carefree life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good disposition or good nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative moral use; the expression contrasting a departing good disposition with an arriving bad one is proverbial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sack or large bag for straw and similar material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical source treats this as an Arabicized or borrowed word and distinguishes it from the vulgar variant in pronunciation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deceiving, beguiling, or causing someone to desire what is vain or false; a deceiver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial or adjectival description of the agent of deception.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Negligent, inattentive, inadvertent, heedless, or unprepared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate adjectival branch related to inexperience and lack of vigilance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rough or rattling sound like that produced by gargling water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A sound noun associated with the reduplicated throat action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sound of a cooking pot when it boils.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred sound description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The repeated movement or rattling of the spirit in the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physiological and death-related sound noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imitative word for the cry of a pastor or a similar sound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An onomatopoeic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most negligent, inattentive, heedless, or unprepared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An elative adjectival form of the negligence branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White or fair in appearance; applied to a person, thing, or group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a white countenance, white people, and the expression for bright or white days.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse or camel, possessing a white forehead blaze or other غُرَّة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is used for a female animal; the blaze may have several recognized shapes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain black bird with a white head, applied to either sex.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological use derived from the color sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man, having a beard covering nearly the whole face except for a small area.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative appearance-based use likening the face to a marked forehead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Generous, illustrious, eminent, noble, or chief among one's people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or woman of rank; the meaning is a figurative extension of conspicuous excellence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely hot or sun-bright, especially of a day or the heat of midday.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use associated with brightness and the force of the sun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year in which there is no rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An assumed-tropical adjectival use recorded in a related lexical citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel having little or lost milk, or one that draws up her milk after previously yielding it freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The loss or withholding may be attributed to fright, disease, dislike of the young, or another cause.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Niggardly or tenacious in withholding what is held, especially of a hand or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of a she-camel withholding milk.

cautions: The Lane entry uses the contracted root spelling غر for this geminate QAC root; the QAC root and forms are retained as canonical.
Lane Quran citations such as [lxxxii. 6] are preserved only as lexical evidence; modern Quran locations in examples are taken from the supplied QAC occurrences, not reconstructed from Lane notation.
غَرُور in the Quran is reported with both a personal-deceiver interpretation, especially the devil, and a worldly-life or worldly-advantage interpretation.
The reported Form IV meanings of emboldening and causing peril are qualified in the lexical evidence by a disputed interpretation of the supporting poetic line.
The technical meaning of غُرَّة in fetal compensation and the exact extent of ritual washing associated with غُرَّة have variant explanations in the lexical evidence.
